AttrValue.description: A scalar attribute value. Deliberately flat — `attrs` is not a document store.

CanonVer.description:
Version of the canonicalisation ruleset that produced a subject hash.

Stamped per subject rather than per record: a re-keyed record can legitimately carry subjects
resolved under different rulesets. Lookups fan out across live versions.

CorrelatedPair.description:
One correlated pair: a record, and a record that followed it inside the window.

Two structures rather than two identifiers, and a pair rather than a flat set. Which decline went
with which deploy *is* the answer — a flat list of both sides is what `GET /records` already gives
a caller, and it cannot say what happened near what once either side matches more than once.

left.description: The record the question was asked about: the earlier of the two.

right.description: The record that followed it, at or after `left` and no later than `within_ms` after.

DataClass.description: Whether a record's body is erasable.

oneOf.description: System and operational activity. Body stored in plaintext.
Traceable to a data subject. Body sealed; erasable by destroying subject keys.

EntityRef.description:
A reference from a record to an entity, with the role the entity played.

Unknown fields are refused for the reason `ActionRecord` refuses them: an entity reference is
a join key, and a field that silently vanished here would leave the record joining on something
other than what was sent.

confidence.description:
Extraction confidence. Below `1.0` means inferred from text rather than a structured field.

The bound is published because `ActionRecord::validate` enforces it: a caller that can read
the schema can fail before sending rather than after.

role.description: How the entity relates to the record.

EntityRole.description: The part an entity plays in a record.

oneOf.description: The record is chiefly about this entity.

Outcome.description: How the outcome of an action is reported.

oneOf.description: The action did what it set out to do.
It partly succeeded, and the record says how.
It was refused, by us or by a downstream system.

RecordId.description: A ULID, and the write's idempotency key. Crockford base32: uppercase, without `I`, `L`, `O` or `U`, so a transcription slip cannot turn one valid identifier into another.

RecordStructure.description:
One record as a read returns it: every frontmatter key, and no body.

Deserialised from the frontmatter a record was stored with rather than rebuilt from parts, so a
read describes the record on disk and not this build's idea of it. Unknown fields are refused for
the reason `ActionRecord` refuses them: a stored key this type does not declare is one nothing
downstream reads, and passing it through would forward whatever the store happened to hold.

agent_ver.description: Agent version, for attributing behaviour to a release.

at.description: Source-reported time. May be skewed; never used for ordering.

attrs.description:
Declared, classified attributes. Structural keys only — a sensitive one is refused on write,
so it is not in frontmatter to be read back.

backfilled.description: `true` when `received_at` came from an upstream source rather than the service's clock.

correlation_id.description: Ties every stage of one interaction together.

data_class.description: Whether the body is erasable. Reported so a caller knows what it is *not* being given.

received_at.description: Time stamped by the service. Authoritative for ordering and windowing.

record_id.description: Identity the record is addressable by.

redaction_policy.description: Redaction policy applied before the write.

schema_ver.description: Schema version the record was written under.

subjects.description: Data subjects named by this record, as keyed pseudonyms. Never a direct identifier.

visibility.description: Read scope the record was stored under.

SchemaVer.description: Version of the record schema a row was written under.

SubjectHash.description: Keyed pseudonym for an erasable data subject — an HMAC over a canonical subject identifier, never a direct identifier, so it is safe in paths, indexes and tombstones. Pseudonymous, not anonymous: whoever holds the keying secret can still relink it. Hex is lowercase, because one spelling per hash is what lets it serve as both a map key and a path component with no normalisation step a caller could forget.

SubjectRef.description:
One data subject named by a record.

Unknown fields are refused for the reason `ActionRecord` refuses them: a field this type does
not declare is one nothing downstream will ever read.

SubjectRole.description: The part a subject plays in a record.

oneOf.description: Named in the record without being its principal.

The actor only.

Stored apart: a subtree of its own per owner, whose directories and files admit no group or
other access. The two halves cover each other — a scoped read answers nothing to anybody
else, and a reader on the host cannot go around the query by opening the file unless it is
the identity the writer runs as.
Audit records. Readable only by the operator role.

description:
Answer to a correlation.

Its own shape rather than a `RecordsResponse`, because the pairing is the answer: flattened into
one `records` list it would be a set of records the caller has to re-join by timestamp, which is
the arithmetic this endpoint exists to stop doing by hand.

pairs.description:
Matching pairs. Newest left record first, and within one left record its right ones in the
order they happened.

token_estimate.description:
Rough token cost of this answer, advisory only.

Measured over both halves of every pair, so a left record matching several right ones is
counted once per pair — which is what returning it once per pair costs.
